title: Cold rebuild: Streaks
summary: Rebuild Streaks from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Streaks** in *Gaps, islands and data quality*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

code: SELECT day, date(day, '-' || ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY day) || ' days') AS grp
SELECT MIN(day), COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY grp ORDER BY 1;
setup: CREATE TABLE app_logins (member TEXT, day TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (member, day));
CREATE TABLE invoices (no INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, issued TEXT);
steps.explain: Ben's days are the 2nd, then the 4th to the 7th: two islands.

steps.title: Rebuild Streaks cold
prompt: Return every streak: **member**, **start**, **finish** and **days**, sorted by member then start.
Tables: `app_logins(member, day)` (one row per member per day they opened the app) and `invoices(no, issued)`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
